title: Feedback Granulator — Priority Slipstream (June 2026)
content:
Purpose: rough distillation of customer field notes + prioritized, low-effort feature patches we can probe in the next 6 weeks. This is intentionally granular — we want tiny bets that reduce customer friction and give measurable telemetry.

Context: pulled from CS triage, a handful of CSM calls (late May), and debug threads from infra on kv-cache misses. Pattern: high-value customers see intermittent latency spikes (p99) tied to cold KV-caches + mixed-model routing; many requests are short-turnaround inference ( <300 tokens) but suffer from batching policies tuned for higher throughput. Several customers asked for either a toggle to reduce batching or an option to pin requests to a low-latency lane. Other asks: visibility (which requests hit cache vs fall back), better default quantization notes in SDK, and a simple per-API-key cost-sensitivity control.

Quick summary of prioritized items (MVP ordering):

1) "cache-hit telemetry" flag (low-effort) — High impact, low infra complexity
   - What: per-request header + dashboard column showing cache hit/miss and KV-cache age (ms). Expose via Console and a stream field in hosted logs.
   - Why: customers want to know if latency is caused by cache warming vs model slowdown. Many current support tickets ask for this before we surface a deep-dive.
   - Implementation notes: add boolean flag in runtime (default off), log event for hit/miss with TTL bucket. Console change: add column to route dashboard. Estimated effort: infra 2d, console 1d, product QA 1d.
   - Metrics to observe: change in p99 for flagged requests, support ticket volume mentioning "cache".

2) "latency-lane" routing profile (experiment) — Medium effort
   - What: allow customers to opt-in a route/api-key into a low-batching, low-concurrency lane (sacrifices throughput/cost for latency). Toggle via API + Console.
   - Why: solves immediate need for OLTP-style apps that require <100ms p95 for short prompts. Several customers reported being forced to self-host because we lacked this knob.
   - Implementation notes: add routing policy with batch size 1..4, strict cpu/gpu concurrency cap, preemptive allocation. Requires release-engineering changes and e2e tests. Estimate: infra 2w, console + docs 3-4d.
   - Success metric: customer adoption and reduction in churn-risk P0 accounts.

3) "per-key cost-sensitivity" (product/ops) — Low-medium effort
   - What: slider in Console + API param for cost vs quality preference. Changes model selection (e.g., quantized vs full), routing preference (dedicated vs shared), and optional response-length caps.
   - Why: customers want automated simple tradeoffs without deep infra knowledge. Also helps us steer cost-of-serving for heavy usage.
   - Implementation notes: prototype as config map that maps preferences to a small set of pre-validated profiles. Integrate into Optimize suggestions later. Estimate: product 3d, infra 5d, docs 2d.

4) SDK prompt-annotations for quantization safety (docs + SDK) — Very low effort
   - What: small SDK helper that warns when prompt/response shapes are known to regress with extreme quantization (e.g., long context + sparse attention). 
   - Why: customers drop to lower-quality models when trying to reduce cost; a gentle nudge prevents obvious regressions.
   - Implement: add heuristics, log a warning + link to console docs. Estimated: SDK 2d, docs 1d.

5) "canary warmers" for KV-cache (ops pattern) — Ops playbook + tiny infra change
   - What: thin canary requests issued on model rollout/scale-up to prefill KV-cache for heavy routes. Customer-visible toggle to enable in route config.
   - Why: avoids cold-cache latency spikes at time of burst. Some customers (search/rerank pipelines) have severe spikes when we evict or scale.
   - Implement: small task queue that emits synthetic prefixes. Est: infra 1w, ops playbook 2d.

Customer vignettes (short, anonymized):
- "AdSearchCo": heavy reranking traffic, 90% of calls <= 180 tokens. Observed p99 jumps when Dedicated pool scales down after quiet hours. Would pay for 'latency-lane' but asked for visibility first.
- "NotesApp": chat-style app; user complaints around occasional 800ms+ replies. Want toggle to prefer lower-batch latency for specific user segments. Also requested per-route spending guardrails.
- "FinData": bank prototyping private deployment; top ask was deterministic rollout (pin model version) + audit for key route latency. Also raised concerns about quantization docs.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- How much throughput do we lose at scale if N customers move to latency-lane? Need SRE sim.
- Is cache-hit telemetry safe to expose (PII?) — ensure logs are scrubbed and only show hashed request ids.
- Rolling canary warmers could increase cost if misconfigured; provide sensible defaults and caps.

Quick experiments to run (1–2 week cycles):
- Experiment A: enable cache-hit telemetry for 3 pilot customers (AdSearchCo, internal dev org, partner X). Measure p99 delta and support ticket correlation.
- Experiment B: spin up latency-lane on internal perf lab; replay short-turnaround traces and observe throughput drop. Simulate 5% of traffic moved to lane and measure cost.
- Experiment C: SDK quantization warnings in next SDK minor release for 1 week, track how often warnings are surfaced and correlate with customers downgrading model.

Notes to self (action items):
- DM SRE (Ravi) for simulation inputs: need realistic short-turnaround traces + eviction patterns.
- Draft short FAQ for CSMs: "What hit/miss means" and "How to request a latency lane".
- File a lightweight RFC for latency-lane policy (scope: routing only; not billing rework).

Telemetry KPIs to add to Console (minimum):
- % requests with cache-hit true per route
- avg/median/95/99 latency for cache-hit vs cache-miss
- cost per 1M tokens for latency-lane vs default

Slack refs / tickets pulled into this doc:
- slack: #cs-field-notes thread 2026-05-29 (AdSearchCo p99 thread)
- jira: JIRA-CUST-1140 (NotesApp complaint thread)
- github: PR 54 in kv-cache-experiments (warmers prototype)

Closing thought: prioritize visibility (cache-hit telemetry + console) first — it is low friction and improves signal for every later change. Latency-lane is the product hook that can differentiate us for OLTP apps, but it needs SRE modelling and an explicit cost story.

Draft messaging for pilot customers (short):
- Subject: "Small telemetry pilot to reduce p99 spikes — opt-in"
- Body: "We're piloting a lightweight cache-hit telemetry flag that will help us identify when latency is caused by cold cache vs model slowness. Opting in will add a 'cache_hit' column to your route logs for 2 weeks. We'll use the data to tune warmers and routing — no change to billing. Reply if you'd like to join. — Aisha"

End of notes. TODO: convert into compact RFC + onboarding checklist if experiments show signal within 2 weeks.
